rationale: This is a platform ToS rather than a digital-goods storefront, and it is unusually direct about content ownership ('What's yours is yours'), so it scores low on ownership opacity; but it pairs that with an extremely broad, royalty-free, sublicensable content license granted for 'no compensation,' an any-time/any-reason termination clause, a $100 liability cap, and dense boilerplate repeated twice for different jurisdictions that burdens readability.
evidence_quotes: What's yours is yours — you own your Content
the use of the Services by you is hereby agreed as being sufficient compensation for the Content and grant of rights herein
We may suspend or terminate your account or cease providing you with all or part of the Services at any time for any or no reason
shall not exceed the greater of one hundred U.S. dollars ($100.00) or the amount you paid Twitter
